layout.window: the app window inside the system insets (status bar, navigation bar, display cutout; not the soft keyboard), width and height in dp (pt on iOS), read again on every configuration change (rotation, resize, text setting)
layout.font_scale: the platform's text scale factor (1.0 at the default text setting)
layout.mode: regular when width / font_scale >= min_width_dp and height / font_scale >= min_height_dp; compact otherwise
layout.home_regular: the header, the trust line, the search row and the floor row have their natural height; the results region and the map share the height that is left 2:3; the result list scrolls inside its region
layout.home_compact: the home screen is one vertical scroll container: every block has its natural height, every result row is laid out, and the map is min(max_height_dp, max_window_fraction x window height) high
layout.other_screens: one vertical scroll container below the header in both modes
layout.header: the title and the actions home.lang, home.qr and home.settings stay shown and operable at every registered window size and text setting; the actions never take the title's width: when they do not fit beside it they move to the next line (B, C). A uses the Material app bar, which keeps one line and shortens the title with an ellipsis; the full title stays in the accessibility tree
layout.mode_change: keeps the query, the results, the selected floor, the computed route and the screen stack; the map view may be created again and its camera may return to the home view
layout.vectors: mode_vectors: [width, height, font_scale, mode]; map_height_vectors: [window height, compact map height]; pinned by the unit tests of A, B and C together with the constants

map_inspect_settle.rule: The same procedure in every candidate: after one frame the reading is taken and repeated every interval_ms until two consecutive readings report the same rendered features (the same entries in the same order) and either at least one feature is rendered or no style is loaded (settled = true), or until bound_ms have passed since the first reading began (settled = false; a reading in progress completes). An unavailable map is written at once (one reading). The harness evaluates the last reading and records passes, elapsed_ms and settled as facts of the case; settled = false is not a finding by itself.

lab_hooks.platform_scope: commands without "platforms" exist on Android and iOS; "platforms": ["android"] marks the hooks of the Android-only harness case families (the iOS scope is build and simulator feasibility)

route_steps.rule: Input: the PATH node sequence of G1-ROUTE-1.0, graph.json and the destination. Walk along the path edges (directed edge from->to) accumulating length for corridor, spur, outdoor and entrance edges. An entrance edge first adds its length, flushes the walk, then emits {kind: exit, building} (indoor -> outdoor, building of the indoor node) or {kind: enter, building} (outdoor -> indoor, building of the indoor node). A stairs or elevator edge flushes the walk and emits {kind: stairs|elevator, floor} with the floor of the next node. At the end the walk is flushed and {kind: arrive, code} is emitted with the destination code. Flushing emits {kind: walk, m} only when the accumulated length is above 0 mm; m = floor((mm + 500) / 1000). Summary {length_m, steps, floors}: length_m = floor((length_mm + 500) / 1000) of the whole route (every edge, stairs and lifts included), steps = number of steps including arrive, floors = floors of the path nodes in first-visit order without repeats (nodes without a floor skipped) joined by "-".

ui_session_script.rule: The script repeats every cycle_s from the window start for warmup_s + measure_s; camera moves use the binding's animated camera API with the given duration; rotation and tilt stay 0.

search_route.order: 500 queries of query_corpus.json in file order, then the 30 cases of route_cases.json in file order, one process, no restart
search_route.search_path: the query text is placed in the search field state and shown (one frame), the loop yields to an idle point (no timed handler starts inside a frame callback: A zero-duration timer, B setTimeout 0, C Android Handler.post on the main looper, C iOS DispatchQueue.main.async) and the same submit handler as home.search.submit runs; compute_ns = duration of the G1-SEARCH-1.0 call alone; e2e_ns = submit handler entry -> the first frame callback after the frame that applied the result state (frame rule, ready_predicate.frame_rule)
search_route.route_path: origin, destination, step_free and the case blocked edges are set on the route screen state and shown (one frame), the loop yields to an idle point and the same handler as route.compute runs; compute_ns = G1-ROUTE-1.0 plus G1-ROUTE-STEPS-1.0; e2e_ns = handler entry -> the first frame callback after the frame that applied the steps (or the rejection) (frame rule)
search_route.result: out/<run_id>.json {contract: "G1-BENCH-SR-1.0", run_id, kind, app, bundle_version, start_ns, end_ns, search: [{id, outcome, ids, compute_ns, e2e_ns}], route: [{id, outcome, nodes?, length_mm?, steps?, summary?, compute_ns, e2e_ns}]}; G1MARK run.start / run.done

bridge.payload: message i carries bytes [(i*64) mod (65536 - size + 1), +size) of the 64 KiB block = SHA-256("G1-SYNTH|2026091401|bridge-payload|<k>") for k = 0..2047 concatenated (common payloadBlock(), fetched once before the series)
bridge.schedule: open loop: message i is due at t0 + round(i * 1e9 / rate_hz) ns; a late message is sent late and recorded, never skipped or coalesced
bridge.r2n_measured: t_send = nowNanos() on the runtime thread, then the payload crosses the candidate boundary to the common echo (async: echoAsync with the reply delivered back to the runtime thread; sync: echoSync on the runtime thread); the common module records t_entry at the start of the echo; latency = t_entry - t_send; the reply (length << 32 | crc) is checked against the runtime CRC-32 of the payload
bridge.r2n_control: t_send = nowNanos(), then a runtime-local echo (t_entry = nowNanos() at its start, copy into a preallocated runtime buffer, CRC-32 written in the runtime language) is called directly on the runtime thread; latency = t_entry - t_send
bridge.n2r_measured: the native worker emits message i at its due time with t_sent = nowNanos(); the runtime handler reads t_recv = nowNanos() first on the runtime thread, then checks the CRC-32 of the payload; latency = t_recv - t_sent
bridge.n2r_control: a runtime-side timer emits message i at its due time with t_sent = nowNanos() and calls the same handler directly; latency = t_recv - t_sent

boundary.A: MethodChannel g1/native (Uint8List payload) for R2N; EventChannel g1/n2r for N2R; no synchronous path (R2N.64B.sync -> UNSUPPORTED)
boundary.B: TurboModule NativeG1: payload as a base64 string (no binary type at this boundary); synchronous JSI method for R2N.64B.sync; codegen event emitter for N2R
boundary.C: direct call into the common module (Kotlin/Swift), including the hop to the native worker and back to the main thread

bridge.order: control-first: null-control series then measured series; measured-first: the reverse (the harness alternates by run number)
bridge.completion: a series completes when every reply/message has arrived, or fails after 10 s without progress (outcome FAILED with the completed count)
bridge.result: out/<run_id>.json {contract: "G1-BENCH-BRIDGE-1.0", run_id, app, workload, order, messages, rate_hz, outcome OK|UNSUPPORTED|FAILED, series: [{kind: control|measured, t0_ns, send_offsets_ns: [...], latencies_ns: [...], completed, crc_failures}]}; G1MARK run.start / run.done

data_contract_text.G1-SEARCH-1.0: normalize(s): NFKC; Eastern-Arabic (U+0660-0669) and Persian (U+06F0-06F9) digits -> ASCII; remove tatweel (U+0640), Arabic marks U+064B-U+065F and U+0670, and the format characters U+061C, U+200B-U+200F, U+202A-U+202E, U+2060-U+2069, U+FEFF; ASCII A-Z -> a-z only (no other case mapping; O/0 and I/1 never substituted). tokens(s): normalize(s) split at runs of whitespace (U+0009-000D, U+0020, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000) and hyphen-like separators (U+002D, U+2010-U+2015, U+2212); empty tokens dropped. codeKey(s): concatenation of tokens(s) with a-z upper-cased. search(q): no tokens -> NO_MATCH. If codeKey(q) matches ^SB[0-9]+F[0-9]+R[0-9]+$ the result is the destination whose codeKey(code) equals it (UNIQUE_MATCH) or NO_MATCH (no token fallback). Otherwise a destination matches when every query token equals one of its tokens: tokens(name_en), tokens(name_ar), "sb<b>" (lower-cased building), "f<floor>", "r<room_number>", "<room_number>" and the lower-cased codeKey(code). 0 matches -> NO_MATCH, 1 -> UNIQUE_MATCH, more -> AMBIGUOUS; ids in ascending code-unit order; no ranking. Reference: synthetic-data/src/search.mjs; oracle: synthetic-data/out/oracle/search_oracle.json over the bundle query_corpus.json.
data_contract_text.G1-ROUTE-1.0: Graph: graph.json directed edges (each undirected edge "E####" appears as from->to and to->from). route(origin node, destination node = destinations[id].node, step_free, blocked undirected edge ids): blocked edges removed; step_free removes edges with step_free = false (stairs); Dijkstra on integer length_mm. Reachable -> PATH {nodes, length_mm}. Otherwise REJECT_STEP_FREE_UNAVAILABLE if step_free was requested and the destination is reachable without that constraint (same blocked set); else REJECT_BLOCKED if edges were blocked and the destination is reachable without the blocked set (same step_free flag); else REJECT_UNREACHABLE. Ties: prev(v) = the smallest node id u (code-unit order) with dist(u) + len(u, v) = dist(v); the path is read back from the destination through prev. Origin equal to the destination node: PATH with one node and length 0. Reference: synthetic-data/src/routes.mjs; oracle: synthetic-data/out/oracle/route_oracle.json over the bundle route_cases.json (unique shortest paths).
data_contract_text.G1-STYLE-1.0: style.json of the active verified bundle: every "g1bundle://" prefix is replaced by the file URL of the bundle directory (ending with "/"); for every layer in metadata.runtime_floor_layers the floor comparison ["==", ["get", "floor"], 1] is replaced by the selected floor; for every layer in metadata.runtime_language_layers the text-field becomes ["get", "name_ar"] or ["get", "name_en"] with the app language; the "route" source receives a FeatureCollection with copies of the geometry.geojson LineString features of the path edges (undirected ids; stairs and lift edges have no geometry and are skipped) with their properties, or an empty collection. map_policy applies (rotation and tilt disabled).

update_transfer.client: the candidate's standard HTTP client (A dart:io HttpClient with the lab CA as the only anchor; B React Native networking (XMLHttpRequest); C Android HttpsURLConnection / iOS URLSession, network security configuration)
update_transfer.origin: https://localhost:8443/ only (any other URL is rejected before a request)
update_transfer.redirects: a redirect inside the lab origin may be followed (at most 5 hops); a redirect never causes a cleartext request and never changes the installed bundle unless the response comes from the lab origin (cases NET05, NET06). A: dart:io follows a redirect to any URL, HTTP included, and no platform cleartext policy applies to its sockets, so A turns the client's automatic redirects off and checks the origin of every hop before the request. B: React Native's networking follows redirects in its native client (OkHttp defaults) and the JavaScript layer sees only the final response; the Android network security configuration refuses the cleartext hop. C Android: HttpsURLConnection follows redirects of the same protocol only. Redirects are not exercised on iOS in G1 (the iOS cohort registers no network case)
update_transfer.total_cap: none (the registered N1w profile needs about 45 s for the 2.7 MB synthetic update)
update_transfer.notes: B: XMLHttpRequest has no separate connect phase; its 30 s inactivity watchdog also covers connect and first byte (the lab path refuses or accepts connections immediately). C iOS: URLSession request timeout 30 s covers connect and inactivity (no separate connect timeout).
